title.narrative: Emergency WASH Assistance to Returnees in Maban

description.narrative:
This GBP £75,000 proposed four month rapid response aims to provide urgent humanitarian assistance through emergency latrine construction and hygiene promotion to individuals affected by armed conflict in South Sudan..
The project will build on lessons learnt by CAFOD in previously implemented and ongoing work with the same implementing partner in the target regions. CAFOD and partner- the Catholic Development Office (CDO) have a long term presence in the proposed locations and hold well established community relations and linkages with the relevant stakeholders, including; South Sudan Relief and Rehabilitation Commission (SSRRC) and the local mainline state departments in Maban and Renk.
Expected project outcomes are twofold:
1) To reduce diseases through improved hygiene practices and access to latrines. Feedback from the previous “Emergency and recovery assistance for host communities, returnees and refugees in Maban, Upper Nile State” (SUD089/1E, December 2013 to 31 July 2014) indicated that latrine coverage is still very low and there is more need for intensive hygiene training to facilitate long-term behaviour change. Low cost latrines will be constructed, coupled with house-to-house hygiene promotion, school-based hygiene promotion and soap distribution.
2) To mitigate tensions between refugees, host and returnee communities. By relieving pressure on restricted resources and by linking relief with rehabilitation and development, this project aims to support the 2 communities to coexist in a peaceful manner providing both with sanitation facilities and hygiene promotion. In general, more humanitarian attention has been paid to refugees, resulting in the returnee and host communities feeling that their similar needs are not been supported, supporting returnees and host communities will ensure that there is a balanced humanitarian support and reduce tensions between refugees and returnees/host communities. Upper Nile is one of South Sudan’s worst affected States, from the current conflict. Proposed activities include: Construction of latrines, and hygiene promotion in Maban
